title: The Witchwood Crown
author: Tad Williams
review:
No spoilers.

This is a really interesting one. In a lot of ways I feel like *more* should have happened than it did but that really isn't Tad's style and there's a deliberate slow burn as are most of his books.

It feels like a distorted reflection of the Dragonbone Chair and comes perilously close to retreading similar ground but I think this is very intentional and is done so to explore deep themes on the nature of war and humanity.

This is epic fantasy and there's a lot of new POVs, characters, and locations being setup here as well as thirty years since the end of To Green Angel Tower. The world hasn't stood still. Quite the opposite.

There's also a lot of dark things that happen that I'm a fan of. Feels like a more mature and modern Memory Sorrow and Thorn where he doesn't shy away from violent and complex morality.

If Tad executes well on everything he's set up and the promises he's made this will end up being one of the best fantasy series. Taking a little break from the series but wanting this to marinate in my brain a bit before continuing on to Empire of Grass.
